claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: Use the canonical top-level join decomposition of a connected nonsingleton cograph, whose blocks are the connected components of its complement. A singleton block is exactly a universal vertex. If there are at least two universal vertices, any two form a pairing dominating set because both closed neighborhoods equal V. If there is no universal vertex, every join block has at least two vertices. Choose distinct a,b in one block and c,d in another. Every vertex of the first block belongs to N[c]∩N[d], while every other vertex belongs to N[a]∩N[b]. These two disjoint pairs therefore form a pairing dominating set, so Remark 9 gives equivalence to zero. The exact checker additionally validated the construction in 3,154 qualifying connected components encountered among all labeled cographs through order six.
claims.witness: For at least two universal vertices, pair any two. With no universal vertex, use pairs (a,b) and (c,d) selected from two distinct complement-components as described.
claims.search_method: Canonical cograph join-decomposition proof, followed by exhaustive labeled-cograph generation and direct verification of the pairing coverage condition.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: Let u be the unique universal vertex of an untouched component C. Swapping u with any proposed move x proves dominance: for Maker, if simulated u ends with Breaker then the simulated contribution of C is zero, whereas the swapped contribution is nonnegative; otherwise both u and x end with Maker and the terminal coloring is unchanged. The reversed inequality proves Breaker's dominance. If Breaker takes u, every closed neighborhood contains a Breaker vertex, making the residual position a zero summand. If Maker takes u, then |C-u|≥2. Every nontrivial cograph has twins (by induction over union/join construction); preassigning one twin to Maker and one to Breaker via Theorem 13 spoils u, while happiness of every residual vertex is exactly its happiness in C-u. The same argument remains valid in any disjoint context, so this is game equivalence, not merely equality of standalone scores. Recursion yields the stated forest game. Conversely, map a prize leaf to K1 and an internal node to K1 joined with the disjoint union of its child graphs and a K2 zero ballast. This is a cograph, preserves the open/delete options, and uses L+3I vertices for L prize leaves and I internal nodes. Exact minimax matched the reduction on all 6,039 labeled cographs of orders one through six and on 21 independently constructed inverse-reduction forest instances.
claims.witness: Forward certificate: unique universal u becomes an internal root and C-u becomes its child forest. Reverse certificate: T maps to K1 ∨ (K2 ⊔ child(T1) ⊔ ... ⊔ child(Tk)).
claims.search_method: Strategy transposition, twin-pair application of Theorem 13 in arbitrary disjoint contexts, inductive inverse construction, and exact exhaustive graph/forest minimax comparison.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Let A be a prize leaf and Z the zero game. Two copies of A have score one for either starter and hence form the constant-one game. For an internal node, discard Z-children and count its A-children. With zero A-children the node has scores (0,0), hence is Z. With one, Maker opening leaves Breaker on A and scores zero, while Breaker deletes the node, again giving (0,0), so it is Z. With two, Maker opening reaches the constant-one game and Breaker deleting reaches zero; these are exactly A's two options. Bottom-up induction therefore assigns every binary-outdegree subtree type A or Z. If z roots have type A, the forest scores are ceil(z/2) and floor(z/2), according to the starter. Cotree reduction and this traversal are linear. Exact forest minimax agreed on 9,295 generated one- and two-tree contexts of total size at most ten.
claims.witness: The complete transition table by number of A-children is 0→Z, 1→Z, 2→A; a forest of z surviving A-roots has scores ((z+1)//2,z//2).
claims.search_method: Induction on rooted subtrees using game equivalence and exact enumeration of bounded-binary typed rooted forests and contexts.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Write V_X(S,l) for the exact value with unopened-star multiset S, l exposed leaves, and player X next. A strong induction on remaining nodes establishes both monotonicity in exposed leaves/star size and the exchange inequality V_X(S∪{j},l+k)≥V_X(S∪{k},l+j) for j≤k and X in {M,B}. The induction maps each exposed-leaf, other-star, and distinguished-star move to its counterpart; opening the distinguished stars produces the identical successor with l+j+k leaves. Consequently Maker loses nothing by opening the largest star, while monotonicity shows Breaker minimizes by deleting the largest star. This yields exactly the displayed two-parameter recurrence. With K equal to the total number of prize leaves, only O(rK) states occur and each takes constant time after sorting, so the bound is O(n^2). Independent unrestricted minimax matched the largest-star recurrence on 856,596 states with up to seven stars, star sizes through 12, and up to 16 initially exposed leaves.
claims.witness: For sorted k1≤...≤kr, the certified optimal star action is kr for either player, yielding M(i,l)=max(1+B(i,l-1),B(i-1,l+ki)) and B(i,l)=min(M(i,l-1),M(i-1,l)), with unavailable leaf terms omitted.
claims.search_method: Simultaneous strong induction proving monotonicity and the star-exchange inequality, plus extended exact unrestricted-versus-restricted minimax enumeration.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: Exact graph minimax gives (Ms,Bs)(P3)=(1,0) and (Ms,Bs)(K1,3)=(1,0), but (Ms,Bs)(P3⊔P3)=(1,1) whereas (Ms,Bs)(P3⊔K1,3)=(2,1). Thus two components with the same proposed state behave differently under the same disjoint-union context. Any compositional cotree dynamic program storing only that pair would identify them and therefore return an incorrect value for one of these unions.
claims.witness: P3 and K1,3 have identical standalone score pairs, while adjoining P3 distinguishes them: P3⊔P3 has (1,1), but P3⊔K1,3 has (2,1).
claims.search_method: Direct exact bitmask minimax on the four concrete graphs, independently cross-checked with the rooted-forest recurrence.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a full classification of SHVG on all cographs by either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness theorem. The draft proves an exact polynomial equivalence to an unrestricted rooted-forest game and gives algorithms only for bounded-binary and height-one reduced forests; it supplies neither an algorithm nor a hardness theorem for arbitrary rooted forests. It therefore does not fully resolve the target. The verified reduction, structural zero classification, two nontrivial tractable subclasses, and state-obstruction are material progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate rather than NO_VALID_PROGRESS. The final writeup expressly says that a complete classification is not obtained and that the unrestricted game remains unresolved. Accordingly its claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE and the headline does not overclaim target coverage.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source JSON and baseline draft JSON; used no web, retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior run, verification report, or other solution.
Reconstructed the terminal SHVG score and both-player minimax using integer bitmasks and exact subset tests; no floating-point decisions were used.
Exhaustively enumerated all 6,039 labeled cographs of orders one through six and compared graph minimax with the independently implemented reduced-forest minimax; all matched.
Explicitly validated 3,154 finite pairing-dominating certificates generated by the structural construction.
Checked 21 representative reverse forest-to-cograph constructions by exact minimax; all matched.
Checked 9,295 bounded-binary rooted-forest contexts against the A/Z bottom-up classification; all matched.
Compared unrestricted and largest-star height-one minimax on 856,596 states; all matched.
